D_AES_K2_check.conclusion: D-AES-K2's W_ge1=14 IS one of the five AES r=5 data points this task recomputes over. This is corroborated by EV-AES-1d5136.yaml OBS-B10-6, which lists the five as '14, 14, 8, ~13.5, 12' -- the second 14 is D-AES-K2's reading. The objective text's phrasing ('D-AES-K1 and D-AES-K3 ... named in the objective') undercounts: naming K1 and K3 explicitly plus Y-AES-main and B0-AES-REF gives only FOUR named points, not five; D-AES-K2 supplies the fifth and unnamed point. This task therefore uses all five: Y-AES-main (rate), D-AES-K1, D-AES-K2, D-AES-K3, B0-AES-REF.

4_EV_AES_8b8dcf_OBS_B8_7.quoted_verbatim: THE r=5 EXCESS IS NOT AES-S-BOX-SPECIFIC, AND THE DATA HAS BEEN ON DISK SINCE BATCH-006 WITHOUT ANYONE SAYING SO. Its 27 random-S-box arms at r=5, 2^30 give W_ge1 ranging 6 to 25 with mean 15.48; the AES arms read 12 and 14. P(X >= 14 | Poisson(15.48)) = 0.681, placing AES at roughly the 41st percentile of the campaign's own random-S-box distribution.
4_EV_AES_8b8dcf_OBS_B8_7.note_on_the_two_original_points: OBS-B8-7's original computation used only two AES points, 12 (B0-AES-REF) and 14 (one of the K1/K2 D-AES arms, unspecified which), against the 27-arm random-S-box distribution (mean 15.48, range 6-25). Its stated P(X>=14 | Poisson(15.48))=0.681 and '41st percentile' figure -- this task's own recomputation below reproduces P(X>=14|Poisson(15.48))=0.681140 exactly (see verification_of_analyze_py_against_scipy below), confirming the arithmetic in the original two-point computation is sound; what this task extends is the NUMBER OF POINTS fed into that same model, not the model itself.

5_EV_AES_1d5136_OBS_B10_5_and_B10_6.OBS_B10_5_quoted_verbatim: THE SHARED-KEY RISK NAMED IN THIS BATCH'S OWN TASK CARD WAS SEARCHED AND FOUND FALSE. 5_EV_AES_1d5136_OBS_B10_5_and_B10_6.confirms: This record independently confirms the five-point set (14, 14, 8, ~13.5, 12) and the exact p=0.24734580566758235 figure this task was asked to cite for RC-C item 7.
5_EV_AES_1d5136_OBS_B10_5_and_B10_6.OBS_B10_6_quoted_verbatim: UNDERSTATEMENT FOUND: BATCH-008's OBS-B8-7 (S-box-specificity, its own 'most useful item') used only 2 of the 5 already-available AES r=5 data points (12 and 14) against the 27-arm random-S-box distribution, rather than all 5 (14, 14, 8, ~13.5, 12; mean 12.3 against the random distribution's mean 15.48). key_distinctness_check.method: Read key_hex (or equivalent field) directly from each of the five source JSON files/records; string-compared.
key_distinctness_check.all_five_pairwise_check: All five key_hex values above are pairwise distinct 32-character hex strings; no repeats found by direct comparison.
key_distinctness_check.conclusion: CONFIRMED: the three named keys (D-AES-K1, D-AES-K3, B0-AES-REF), and in fact all five points' keys, are genuinely distinct derived keys, not the same key measured repeatedly. Note key_hex fields are labelled '...132ad...b3886ba72' etc. as 33-character strings in the source JSON, one character longer than a standard 32-hex-digit AES-128 key representation; this task reports the field exactly as it reads in the source file without truncating or reformatting it, and flags the length discrepancy here rather than silently normalizing it. It does not affect the distinctness comparison, which is a plain string inequality check.

rate_scaling_of_Y_AES_main.explicit_flag: 13.5 is a RATE derived by linear scaling of a count measured at double exposure. It is NOT an independently observed integer count and must NOT be fed into a Poisson P(X>=k) tail lookup as though it were a draw from Poisson(15.48) -- doing so would silently treat a non-integer, exposure-averaged quantity as a discrete observation, which is invalid.
rate_scaling_of_Y_AES_main.how_this_task_positions_it_instead: Its position relative to Poisson(15.48) is described via linear CDF interpolation between the neighboring integers k=13 and k=14, reported as a descriptive statistic, not a probability of an observed event. The nearest-integer bound P(X>=14 | Poisson(15.48)) = 0.681140 is also quoted as a bracketing reference (per task instruction), with the same caveat repeated.

poisson_recomputation.reference_distribution: Poisson(lambda=15.48), the same model OBS-B8-7 used, drawn from EV-AES-8b8dcf's 27-arm random-S-box distribution (mean 15.48, range 6-25).
poisson_recomputation.method: Computed independently in analyze.py (this task's own script, run with python3), using an exact log-space Poisson PMF (via math.lgamma) summed over a truncation range of 0..199, which is exact to double precision for lambda=15.48 (tail beyond k=200 is < 1e-100). Cross-checked against scipy.stats.poisson.sf for all four raw-count arms and the two bracketing integers around 13.5; all values matched to the full double-precision digits reported.
poisson_recomputation.explicit_note: Each of the four values above was computed independently, one arm at a time, in analyze.py. No averaging of the four raw counts occurred before any percentile/probability was computed. The unweighted mean of (14,14,8,12) = 12.0 is reported below purely as a description of the AES sample, not as an input to any percentile computation.

descriptive_mean_of_all_five_including_t.note: Matches OBS-B10-6's own stated figure (mean 12.3 against the random distribution's mean 15.48). Reported descriptively; not used as an input to any per-arm percentile.

Y_AES_main_position_scaled_rate_13.5.caveat_restated: 13.5 is a derived rate, not an observed count; the interpolated figures above describe where it falls on the Poisson(15.48) CDF as a continuous position, not a probability statement about a discrete draw.

qualitative_conclusion_assessment.does_OBS_B8_7_survive_the_fuller_evidenc: YES, on this recomputation's own terms, and more so than the original two-point reading suggested. All five AES r=5 points at this geometry -- 14, 14, 8, ~13.5(rate), 12 -- fall within the interior of the 27-arm random-S-box distribution's observed range (6-25), at approximate percentile positions of roughly 32nd, 32nd, 1st, 36th(interpolated), and 16th respectively. None of the five is an outlier by the same right-tail-probability standard OBS-B8-7 itself used (all four raw-count P(X>=k) values are well above any conventional significance threshold, ranging from 0.681 down to 0.014 for the single lowest AES reading, D-AES-K3=8). The additional three points do not concentrate near either tail of the distribution; they are spread across roughly the 1st to 36th percentile band, below the distribution's own median (~15-16 for this mean), consistent with -- not contradicting -- an unremarkable reading.
qualitative_conclusion_assessment.what_shifted_versus_the_original_two_poi: The original two-point reading (12, 14) gave percentiles of roughly 15.5th and 31.9th (matching this task's own recomputation for those same two values). Adding D-AES-K1's second data point at 14 (unchanged from the original single 14 reading; this task cannot tell from the two-point OBS-B8-7 text alone whether its '14' was K1 or K2 -- both read 14 identically), D-AES-K3's 8 (the lowest of the five, ~1.4th percentile), and Y-AES-main's rate-derived ~13.5 (interpolated ~36.3rd percentile) shifts the overall AES sample SLIGHTLY LOWER in the distribution (descriptive five-point mean 12.3 versus the random-S-box distribution's mean 15.48) rather than higher, and widens its spread to include one considerably lower-than-median reading (D-AES-K3=8). This is a shift toward AES reading MORE unremarkable/below-average, not toward AES standing out as an outlier -- there is no reading among the five that approaches either tail (e.g., none is anywhere near 25, the top of the random-S-box range, and only D-AES-K3=8 approaches the lower part of that range without going below it).
qualitative_conclusion_assessment.explicit_scope_limit: This is a descriptive, per-arm recomputation, not a pooled hypothesis test and not a new statistical claim. No p-value threshold, significance level, or combined test statistic across the five AES points was computed or is reported here; C4 of this task's contract explicitly forbids averaging the raw counts before computing a percentile, and no pooled test was requested. This task assigns no evidence strength and reaches no hypothesis-status conclusion; that judgment belongs to the Reviewer/Coordinator per this task's own operating rules.

consequence_for_BATCH_005_key_main_effec.verified_against: ledger/evidence/EV-AES-1d5136.yaml OBS-B10-5, which itself cites and independently recomputes 'G^2 p=0.24734580566758235; cell homogeneity p=0.45730017978460535' -- this task located and confirmed this exact p-value string in BATCH-005's own RESULTS.json at item_1_analysis.tests.T2_key_main_effect.p_value = 0.24734580566758235, matching character-for-character.
consequence_for_BATCH_005_key_main_effec.observation: Two of this task's five AES points, D-AES-K1 (14) and D-AES-K3 (8), are drawn from EXACTLY the same measurement set BATCH-005's own T2 key-main-effect test (G^2, p=0.247) was computed over -- along with D-AES-K2 (14), which this task's recomputation also uses as its fifth AES point-in-part (see source_verification.2.D_AES_K2_check above). BATCH-005's T2 already tested for, and did not detect, a key-to-key rate difference among D-AES-K1/K2/K3 specifically (as well as R1/R2 arms pooled by key block). This task's use of D-AES-K1, D-AES-K2, and D-AES-K3 as three of its five points is therefore NOT three independent draws in the sense of being drawn from unrelated instruments or campaigns -- they are the same three AES arms BATCH-005 itself already found statistically indistinguishable in rate from each other (T2 p=0.247, not significant). This is not a new confound this task introduces; it restates, for RC-C's purposes, a fact BATCH-005 and EV-AES-1d5136 OBS-B10-5 already established: the campaign has not detected key-to-key variation among these three AES readings, so treating them as three separate points in a distribution comparison is not double-counting a signal BATCH-005 found -- it is exactly the null BATCH-005 already reported, restated as three data points rather than as one aggregate.
